checklist.step: Confirm the critical business service inventory and the year's test scope
actions: Pull the current critical-service inventory from the BCP register and confirm each service still has a named business owner and a technology recovery dependency mapped in the CMDB.
Ask each business owner to reconfirm the service's criticality tier and its board-approved RTO/RPO for the coming cycle.
Flag any service added or retired since the last cycle and add or remove it from this year's test scope accordingly.
Publish the confirmed scope list to the Disaster Recovery Manager and the Operational Resilience Lead.
checklist.done: the test scope lists every current critical service with an owner, an RTO/RPO target and a CMDB dependency mapping.

checklist.step: Design severe-but-plausible test scenarios for the cycle
actions: Draw candidate scenarios from the current ORSA/DCAT severe-but-plausible scenario set plus recent sector incident intelligence (ransomware, data centre loss, key third-party outage).
For each in-scope critical service pick at least one scenario that forces a full technology failover, not just a tabletop walk-through.
Circulate the draft scenario list to the Chief Information Officer and the Operational Resilience Lead for sign-off before scheduling.
Record the approved scenario set and its rationale in the test plan document.
checklist.done: every critical service has an approved, failover-forcing test scenario tied to the ORSA/DCAT scenario set.

checklist.step: Stand up the isolated test environment and freeze the test window
actions: In ServiceNow open a Change Request for the test window and attach the approved scenario list.
Provision the isolated recovery environment from the CMDB build reference and confirm it matches the production recovery configuration.
Notify affected application owners and the IT Service Delivery Manager of the test window and any expected service impact.
Lock the test window in the shared resilience test calendar to prevent conflicting change activity.
checklist.done: an approved change ticket exists, the recovery environment is provisioned to spec, and the test window is locked with no conflicting changes.

checklist.step: Execute the failover/recovery test for each critical service
actions: Trigger the failover per the approved scenario and runbook, timestamping the start of the outage/failover event.
Record every manual intervention step taken outside the documented runbook, with who performed it and why.
Confirm the failed-over service is functionally usable by the business owner before declaring recovery complete.
Timestamp full recovery and capture screenshots or logs of the recovered service state.
checklist.done: every scoped service has a timestamped failover start, a logged intervention trail and a business-owner-confirmed recovery.

checklist.step: Measure actual RTO/RPO against the board-approved targets
actions: Compute actual RTO as recovery-confirmed timestamp minus failover-start timestamp for each service.
Compute actual RPO from the last verified good data point before the simulated loss versus the recovered data state.
Compare both figures to the service's board-approved target and mark PASS/FAIL on the results sheet.
Where a FAIL occurs, capture the contributing factor (undersized capacity, stale runbook step, third-party delay) on the row.
checklist.done: every service has a computed actual RTO/RPO, a PASS/FAIL call against target, and a noted contributing factor for any fail.

checklist.step: Log test tickets for every gap in the ITSM platform
actions: For every FAIL row, open a ServiceNow incident/problem ticket linked to the test change record.
Populate the ticket with the service name, target vs actual RTO/RPO, and the noted contributing factor.
Assign the ticket to the technology owner responsible for the failing component and set a due date inside the current quarter.
Link all tickets from the cycle into a single tracking dashboard for the Disaster Recovery Manager.
checklist.done: every FAIL has a linked, assigned ServiceNow ticket with a due date, visible on the cycle tracking dashboard.

checklist.step: Root-cause each failed test before remediation design starts
actions: Convene the technology owner and the Resilience Engineer to walk the failure timeline against the runbook step by step.
Classify the root cause as runbook defect, capacity/configuration gap, third-party dependency failure, or human execution error.
Check whether the same root cause appears in a prior cycle's exceptions; if so, mark it a repeat finding.
Record the classified root cause on the ServiceNow ticket.
checklist.done: every FAIL ticket carries a classified root cause and a repeat-finding flag where applicable.

checklist.step: Draft the remediation plan with named owners and target dates
actions: For each root cause, define the remediation action (runbook rewrite, capacity uplift, contract amendment, retraining) and its owner.
Set a target closure date that allows retest before the next annual cycle; repeat findings get an accelerated date.
Route capacity/configuration remediations to the Disaster Recovery Engineer and contractual remediations to the Third-Party Risk Manager where a vendor is the cause.
Attach the remediation plan to the cycle's ServiceNow tracking dashboard.
checklist.done: every FAIL has a remediation action, an owner and a target date on the tracking dashboard, with repeat findings accelerated.

checklist.step: Escalate material or repeat gaps to the CIO and Operational Resilience Lead
actions: Identify any FAIL on a Tier 1 critical service or any repeat finding from the prior cycle as material.
Brief the Chief Information Officer within five business days of the root-cause session with the material findings and remediation plan.
Decide with the CIO whether the finding requires interim compensating controls before remediation completes.
Record the escalation, the CIO's decision and any compensating control on the finding's ticket.
checklist.done: every material or repeat finding is briefed to the CIO within five business days with a recorded decision on compensating controls.

checklist.step: Update BCP/DR documentation and runbooks from the test findings
actions: Redline every runbook step that failed or required an undocumented manual intervention during the test.
Route the redlined runbook to the relevant technology owner for technical accuracy review.
Version and publish the updated runbook to the BCP document library, retiring the prior version.
Confirm the updated RTO/RPO figures (if targets changed) are reflected in the BCP register.
checklist.done: every runbook touched by a test failure or manual workaround is redlined, reviewed and republished in the BCP library.

checklist.step: Prepare the board reporting package for the cycle
actions: Build the RTO/RPO scorecard summarizing pass/fail counts by criticality tier and by root-cause category.
Summarize material and repeat findings with their remediation status and target dates.
Include the ORSA/DCAT scenario linkage so the board can see resilience testing coverage against the risk assessment.
Route the draft package to the Chief Information Officer for review before the board meeting.
checklist.done: the board package covers the RTO/RPO scorecard, material/repeat findings and the ORSA/DCAT scenario linkage, reviewed by the CIO.

checklist.step: Present results to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the final board package to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the scorecard, material findings and remediation commitments, and take committee questions.
Record the committee's acceptance or any additional direction (e.g. accelerated remediation, added scenario) in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal as the annual resilience test attestation.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the annual resilience test results and any additional direction.

checklist.step: File the cycle evidence and apply retention labelling
actions: Assemble the test plan, execution logs, RTO/RPO results, ServiceNow tickets and board minutes into the cycle evidence folder.
Move the folder into the compliance evidence repository and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the folder is indexed and searchable by critical service name and test year.
Notify the Disaster Recovery Manager that the cycle record is filed and closed.
checklist.done: the cycle evidence folder is filed, retention-labelled and searchable in the compliance evidence repository.

checklist.step: Track remediation tickets to closure before the next cycle opens
actions: Review the open remediation ticket dashboard monthly and chase owners approaching their target date.
Require evidence of the completed fix (updated runbook, capacity change record, amended contract clause) before closing a ticket.
Escalate any ticket that will miss its target date to the Operational Resilience Lead for a revised date or compensating control.
Confirm zero open Tier 1 tickets remain before the next annual test scope is confirmed.
checklist.done: every remediation ticket is closed with evidence, or has an Operational-Resilience-Lead-approved revised date, before the next cycle opens.

checklist.step: Obtain CIO sign-off closing the annual cycle
actions: Review the closure evidence for every remediation ticket raised in the cycle.
Confirm the retention-labelled evidence folder and the board minutes are both filed.
Sign the cycle closure record confirming the annual BCP/DR test obligation is met for the year.
Notify the Operational Resilience Lead that the cycle is formally closed.
checklist.done: the CIO has signed the cycle closure record and the Operational Resilience Lead has been notified.

testing.step: Build the population of critical services and tests due for the cycle
actions: Extract the full critical-service inventory from the BCP register as of the start of the test year.
Extract every DR/failover test event logged against those services in ServiceNow for the year.
Reconcile the two extracts and list any critical service with zero logged tests as an automatic population exception.
Sign the reconciled population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between the BCP register and ServiceNow, with untested services flagged, and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of Tier 1 critical services.
Take a random, seeded sample of at least 25% of remaining critical services, minimum 10 services.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of Tier 1 services.

testing.step: Re-perform the RTO/RPO calculation for each sampled service
actions: Pull the raw failover-start and recovery-confirmed timestamps from the test execution log for each sampled service.
Independently recompute actual RTO and RPO from the raw timestamps without referring to the reported scorecard first.
Compare the recomputed figures to the reported scorecard; any discrepancy beyond a five-minute tolerance is an exception.
Capture the raw log extract into the workpaper as evidence.
testing.done: every sampled service has an independently recomputed RTO/RPO reconciled to the reported scorecard within tolerance.

testing.step: Trace scoring calls to the underlying test evidence
actions: For each sampled PASS, confirm the recovered-service screenshot or log genuinely shows a functioning service, not just a powered-on instance.
For each sampled FAIL, confirm the ServiceNow ticket exists, is assigned, and carries a classified root cause.
Flag any PASS lacking sufficient recovery evidence as a scoring exception.
testing.done: every sampled PASS is evidenced and every sampled FAIL has a linked, root-caused ticket, or the gap is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Check remediation ticket closure evidence for prior-cycle repeat findings
actions: Pull every ticket marked as a repeat finding from the prior cycle.
Confirm each was closed with genuine fix evidence (updated runbook, capacity change, amended contract clause) before this cycle's test.
Confirm the same root cause did not recur in this cycle for any closed repeat finding.
List any repeat finding closed without evidence or that recurred as an exception.
testing.done: every prior-cycle repeat finding is confirmed genuinely closed and non-recurring, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify escalation and compensating controls on material findings
actions: Pull every finding classified material in the cycle (Tier 1 fail or repeat finding).
Confirm the CIO briefing occurred within five business days of the root-cause session per the recorded timestamp.
Where a compensating control was recorded, confirm it was actually implemented, not just proposed.
List any late briefing or unimplemented compensating control as an exception.
testing.done: every material finding shows a timely CIO briefing and an implemented compensating control where one was recorded, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm the board reporting package matches the underlying results
actions: Open the board portal record of the presented package and compare its scorecard totals to the independently rebuilt population and sample results.
Confirm the minutes reflect the same material findings and remediation commitments as the underlying tracking dashboard.
Flag any figure in the board package that does not reconcile to source data.
testing.done: the board package reconciles to the underlying test population and tracking dashboard, or discrepancies are logged.

testing.step: Recompute the retention and filing status of the cycle evidence
actions: Confirm the cycle evidence folder exists in the compliance evidence repository with the 7-year retention label applied.
Confirm the folder is indexed and retrievable by critical service name and test year within the workpaper's search test.
Flag any missing artifact (test plan, execution log, ticket export, board minutes) as an exception.
testing.done: the evidence folder is confirmed retention-labelled, complete and retrievable, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception with the affected service, what was missed, and the resilience impact.
Assign a root cause (untested service, missing evidence, late escalation, false closure) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next cycle's mandatory retest list.
Confirm no exception is closed without evidence attached.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the annual resilience test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare it to the zero-untested-Tier-1 threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who performed no part of the sample testing sign the workpaper.
Report results and open exceptions to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Assign or reconfirm the criticality tier for every arrangement
actions: Score each arrangement against the B-10 criticality factors: impact of failure on critical business services, substitutability, and data sensitivity.

Route Critical-tier assignments to the Chief Info Security Officer for concurrence.
Flag any tier that changed from the prior cycle and note why.
checklist.done: every arrangement carries a scored, rationale-backed tier in Archer, with Critical tiers concurred by the CISO.

checklist.step: Run the required-clause checklist against each Critical/Material contract
actions: In Icertis CLM open the executed contract and check for the B-10-required clauses: service levels, security requirements, sub-contracting/fourth-party notification, business continuity obligations, audit rights, OSFI access rights, data location, and termination/exit terms.
Mark each clause present/absent on the checklist and paste the exact clause reference (section number) where present.
For any missing clause, open an amendment request to Legal Counsel with the vendor's renewal or amendment window.
Save the completed checklist against the contract record in Icertis.
checklist.done: every Critical/Material contract has a completed clause checklist in Icertis, with amendment requests opened for any gap.

checklist.step: Escalate missing OSFI access and audit-rights clauses
actions: Pull every checklist row marked missing for OSFI access rights or audit rights on a Critical-tier vendor.
Assess whether the vendor relationship can proceed unamended pending contract renewal, or whether an immediate side-letter is required.
Negotiate and execute a side-letter or amendment restoring the clause where the risk cannot wait for renewal.
Record the resolution and its effective date on the contract's Icertis record.
checklist.done: no Critical-tier vendor is missing OSFI access or audit rights without a documented side-letter or an accepted, dated renewal-window remediation.

checklist.step: Confirm sub-contracting/fourth-party notification obligations are current
actions: Request each Critical-tier vendor's current sub-contractor/fourth-party disclosure per the contract's notification clause.
Compare the disclosure to the fourth parties already linked in Archer and add any newly disclosed entity.
Assess the fourth party's own criticality contribution and re-score the primary vendor's tier if it has materially changed.
Log the disclosure date and source document against the vendor record.
checklist.done: every Critical-tier vendor's fourth-party disclosure is current, reconciled to Archer, and re-scored where material.

checklist.step: Assess data location and cross-border transfer terms
actions: Confirm the contract states the jurisdiction(s) where in-scope data is stored and processed.
Compare the stated location(s) to internal data residency policy and flag any non-conforming location.
Where non-conforming, route to Legal Counsel for an amendment or a documented risk acceptance from the Chief Risk Officer.
Record the confirmed data location(s) on the Archer vendor record.
checklist.done: every Critical-tier vendor's data location is confirmed, policy-conforming or risk-accepted, and recorded in Archer.

checklist.step: Review business continuity and exit/contingency provisions
actions: Confirm the contract obligates the vendor to maintain and test its own BCP/DR arrangements and to share test results on request.
Confirm the exit clause specifies a transition assistance period, data return/destruction terms and format, and a maximum transition timeline.
For each Critical-tier vendor, confirm an internal exit plan exists naming an alternate provider or in-house fallback.
Log any vendor missing an exit clause or an internal exit plan as an exception with a remediation date.
checklist.done: every Critical-tier vendor has a contractual BCP obligation, an exit clause, and a documented internal exit plan, or a logged exception.

checklist.step: Set the ongoing monitoring cadence per tier

Attach the monitoring evidence type required per tier (SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, financial health check, SLA performance report).
Assign the monitoring task owner and due date for each vendor in the workflow.
Confirm the workflow auto-escalates a missed monitoring task after 15 days overdue.
checklist.done: every vendor has a tier-appropriate monitoring cadence, evidence type and owner configured with auto-escalation in Archer.

checklist.step: Collect and review the current-cycle monitoring evidence
actions: Request the due monitoring artifact (SOC 2, pen test summary, SLA report) from each vendor per the configured cadence.
Review the artifact for control exceptions, qualified opinions, or SLA breaches and score the vendor's risk rating accordingly.
Route any material control exception to the Chief Info Security Officer for a follow-up assessment.
File the reviewed artifact against the vendor record in Archer with the review date and reviewer.
checklist.done: every due monitoring artifact is collected, reviewed, scored, and filed against the vendor record with material exceptions escalated.

checklist.step: Log register and contract exceptions with disposition

Assign a remediation owner (Contract Administrator, Legal Counsel, or the vendor relationship owner) and a target date.
Set Critical-tier exceptions to a maximum 30-day remediation window; Material-tier to 90 days.
Track open exceptions on the Third-Party Risk Manager's monthly register review.
checklist.done: every register/contract exception has a tracker issue, an owner, a tier-appropriate target date, and monthly tracking.

checklist.step: Brief the Chief Info Security Officer on Critical-tier exceptions

Present the summary to the CISO and obtain a decision on any exception approaching its 30-day window.
Record the CISO's decision (accept residual risk, escalate to General Counsel, or terminate the relationship) on the exception record.
Communicate the decision to the Third-Party Risk Manager for register update.
checklist.done: every Critical-tier exception nearing its window has a recorded CISO decision communicated back to the register owner.

Update the Archer vendor record to reflect the remediated clause, tier or monitoring status.
Close the tracker issue with a reference to the remediation evidence.
Re-run the required-clause checklist on the vendor to confirm no other gap remains.
checklist.done: every remediated exception has evidence attached, the register is updated, and the checklist re-confirms no residual gap.

Sign the annual register refresh attestation.
Notify the Third-Party Risk Manager and General Counsel that the refresh is closed for the cycle.
checklist.done: the CISO has signed the annual register refresh attestation with zero unresolved Critical-tier exceptions.

Apply the 7-year-from-termination retention label to each vendor's evidence package.

Notify the CISO that the cycle evidence is filed.
checklist.done: the finalized register and supporting evidence are filed, retention-labelled and searchable by vendor and tier.

Present the summary and record the committee's acceptance or any additional direction in the minutes.

checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the annual third-party risk register status.

Compare the located clause references to the checklist on file; any missing or misattributed clause is an exception.

testing.done: every sampled contract's clause checklist is independently verified against the actual clause text, or discrepancies are logged.

testing.step: Confirm monitoring evidence currency for the sample

Flag any overdue or unreviewed monitoring artifact as an exception.

Confirm the plan names a specific alternate provider or in-house fallback and a transition timeline consistent with the contract's exit clause.

testing.done: every sampled closed exception is confirmed genuinely remediated, or a false-closure exception is logged.

testing.done: every Critical-tier exception's aging is recomputed and any window breach is either decision-backed or logged as a control failure.

Assign a root cause (stale contract, missed monitoring, false closure, mis-tiering) and an owner.

testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Detect and open a case for every candidate security/technology event
actions: Monitor SIEM/SOAR alert queues and open a case for any alert meeting the severity-2-or-higher trigger criteria.
Capture the detection timestamp, affected system(s) and initial indicators in the case record.
Notify the Incident Response Lead immediately for any alert touching a critical business service or customer data.
Preserve the raw log/alert evidence before any remediation action alters system state.
checklist.done: a timestamped SOAR case exists for the event with preserved raw evidence and the Incident Response Lead notified where critical scope is touched.

checklist.step: Triage the event against OSFI's reportability criteria
actions: Assess the event against OSFI's material-impact and high-potential-impact factors: extent of disruption, data sensitivity, customer/counterparty impact, and duration.
Record the reportability determination (reportable / not reportable / monitor) and the assessment timestamp on the case.
Where reportable, start the 24-hour notification clock from the determination timestamp, not the original detection time.
Brief the Chief Info Security Officer within one hour of a reportable determination.
checklist.done: every candidate event has a timestamped, documented reportability determination, with the notification clock started for reportable events.

checklist.step: Assemble the initial OSFI notification content
actions: Draft the notification covering: nature and cause (if known), date/time of detection and of the reportability determination, systems and services affected, and immediate containment actions taken.
State whether customer data or third-party services are implicated and the current containment status.
Route the draft to the Chief Info Security Officer and, where customer data is implicated, to the General Counsel for review.
Finalize the notification text before the 24-hour clock expires.
checklist.done: the notification draft is complete, reviewed and finalized inside the 24-hour window from the reportability determination.

checklist.step: Submit the initial notification to OSFI and log the confirmation
actions: Send the initial notification to OSFI through the institution's designated supervisory contact channel, copying the Board Governance Lead.
Record the exact submission timestamp against the case, and compute elapsed hours from the reportability determination.
Confirm the elapsed time is within 24 hours; if not, immediately open a late-notification exception.
File the sent notification and any delivery confirmation in the case record.
checklist.done: the notification is submitted, its elapsed time from determination is computed and confirmed within 24 hours or logged as a late-notification exception.

checklist.step: Establish the follow-up reporting cadence
actions: Confirm with OSFI (or infer from the advisory's default expectation) the required follow-up update frequency for the incident's severity.
Schedule follow-up update tasks in the ITSM case system at the agreed cadence until closure.
Assign each follow-up task an owner responsible for gathering the latest containment/remediation status.
Set an auto-escalation if a scheduled follow-up task is not completed within 24 hours of its due time.
checklist.done: a follow-up cadence is scheduled with owned, auto-escalating tasks through to incident closure.

checklist.step: Investigate root cause and quantify impact
actions: Perform forensic analysis on affected systems to establish root cause, entry vector and scope of compromise.
Quantify impact: number of customers/records affected, duration of service disruption, and any financial exposure.
Update the case record with findings as they firm up, without waiting for full closure to share materially new information.
Flag any material change in scope to the Incident Response Lead so a supplementary OSFI update can be issued.
checklist.done: root cause and quantified impact are documented and any material scope change triggers a supplementary update.

checklist.step: Issue supplementary updates to OSFI as new material facts emerge
actions: Compare each new forensic finding to what was last reported to OSFI and determine if it is materially new.
Draft and route a supplementary update through the same review chain as the initial notification for any material change.
Log each supplementary update's content and submission timestamp on the case.
Keep the Board Governance Lead copied on all supplementary updates for board awareness.
checklist.done: every materially new fact is reported to OSFI as a logged, timestamped supplementary update.

checklist.step: Coordinate containment and remediation actions
actions: Direct containment actions (isolation, credential reset, patch deployment) and log each action with timestamp and owner.
Confirm with the affected system owner that containment is effective before declaring the incident contained.
Coordinate with the Third-Party Risk Manager where a critical vendor's system is implicated.
Update the case status to Contained, then Remediated, with evidence at each transition.
checklist.done: containment and remediation actions are logged with timestamps and the case status reflects verified containment and remediation.

checklist.step: Prepare the closure report with root cause and lessons learned
actions: Compile the full incident timeline: detection, reportability determination, notification, supplementary updates, containment and remediation.
Document root cause, quantified impact, and control gaps that allowed the incident.
Draft lessons-learned actions with owners, distinguishing technical fixes from process fixes (e.g. detection tuning, playbook updates).
Route the closure report to the Chief Info Security Officer for review.
checklist.done: a closure report with full timeline, root cause, impact and owned lessons-learned actions is drafted and routed for CISO review.

checklist.step: Submit the closure notification to OSFI
actions: Review the closure report for completeness and accuracy against the case record.
Send the closure notification to OSFI confirming remediation is complete and summarizing root cause and lessons learned.
Log the closure notification timestamp and any OSFI acknowledgement received.
Close the incident case once OSFI acknowledgement (or the internal closure SLA) is satisfied.
checklist.done: OSFI closure notification is sent, logged, and the case is closed on acknowledgement or the internal closure SLA.

checklist.step: Log any missed or late notification as a compliance exception
actions: For any notification that exceeded 24 hours or any reportable event not notified, open a compliance exception ticket.
Assign a root cause (triage delay, escalation breakdown, drafting delay) and an owner for the process fix.
Set a remediation date for the process fix and, where appropriate, brief the Board Risk Committee.
Track the exception to closure with evidence of the process fix.
checklist.done: every missed or late notification has a root-caused exception ticket, an owner, a remediation date and tracked closure.

checklist.step: Feed lessons learned back into detection and playbooks
actions: Implement the technical lessons-learned actions (new detection rules, tuning) in the SIEM/SOAR platform.
Update the incident response playbook with any process fix from the closure report.
Confirm the updated detection rule fires correctly in a controlled test before relying on it operationally.
Version and publish the updated playbook to the incident response team.
checklist.done: detection rules and the playbook are updated from lessons learned, with the new detection rule verified operational.

checklist.step: Retain the incident case evidence for the retention period
actions: Export the full case record, notification correspondence, follow-up updates and closure report.
File the export into the compliance evidence repository under the incident id and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by incident id and notification date.
Notify the CISO that the case evidence is filed.
checklist.done: the incident evidence is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by incident id.

checklist.step: Brief the Board Risk Committee on reportable incidents for the period
actions: Summarize every reportable incident for the period: notification timing, root cause, impact and remediation status.
Upload the summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the summary and any missed-notification exceptions, recording committee questions and direction in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the period's reportable incidents and any notification exceptions.

checklist.step: Refresh reportability triage criteria after any advisory update
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to the Technology and Cyber Security Incident Reporting Advisory.
Compare any change to the current triage criteria and notification procedure.
Update the documented procedure and retrain the SOC and incident response teams on any material change.
Record the procedure version update and training completion date.
checklist.done: the triage procedure is current against the latest advisory, with training completion recorded on any material update.

testing.step: Build the population of incidents and near-misses for the quarter
actions: Extract every SOAR case opened in the quarter meeting the severity-2-or-higher trigger, plus every case triaged as potentially reportable.
Reconcile the extract to the ITSM/security ticketing system case list and resolve any count difference before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population as complete.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between SIEM/SOAR and the ITSM case system and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of cases marked reportable to OSFI.
Take a random, seeded sample of at least 25% of non-reportable severity-2+ cases, minimum 10 cases.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of reportable cases.

testing.step: Re-perform the reportability determination for each sampled case
actions: Read the case's raw evidence and independently apply OSFI's material/high-potential-impact criteria without viewing the recorded determination first.
Compare the independent determination to the recorded one; any difference is an exception, including a reportable case marked not reportable.
Capture the independent assessment notes into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled case has an independently re-performed reportability determination reconciled to the record, or an exception logged.

testing.step: Recompute the notification timing against the 24-hour window
actions: For each sampled reportable case, pull the recorded reportability determination timestamp and the notification submission timestamp.
Compute elapsed hours and compare to the 24-hour requirement.
Flag any case exceeding 24 hours, or any case where the determination timestamp appears backdated to avoid a breach, as an exception.
testing.done: notification timing is recomputed for every sampled reportable case, with breaches or suspect timestamps logged.

testing.step: Trace notification content to the case evidence
actions: Compare the sent notification's stated facts (systems affected, containment status, data implicated) to the case record as of the submission time.
Flag any material inaccuracy or omission in what was reported.
Confirm any customer-data-implicated case had General Counsel review before submission.
testing.done: notification content is traced to case evidence for accuracy, with omissions or missing legal review logged.

testing.step: Confirm supplementary updates were issued for material new facts
actions: Review the forensic findings timeline for each sampled reportable case for materially new facts after the initial notification.
Confirm a supplementary update was submitted to OSFI for each material change, with a timestamp.
Flag any material change not reported as an exception.
testing.done: every material post-notification finding traces to a submitted supplementary update, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify closure report completeness and OSFI closure notification
actions: Confirm each sampled case's closure report covers timeline, root cause, quantified impact and lessons learned.
Confirm the OSFI closure notification was sent and logged with a timestamp.
Flag any case closed internally without a corresponding OSFI closure notification.
testing.done: every sampled case has a complete closure report and a logged OSFI closure notification, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Confirm lessons-learned actions were actually implemented
actions: Pull the lessons-learned action list from each sampled case's closure report.
Confirm each technical action (new detection rule, tuning) is live in SIEM/SOAR and each process action is reflected in the current playbook version.
Flag any lessons-learned action left open past its target date.
testing.done: lessons-learned actions are confirmed implemented in the live environment, or open items are flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per testing exception with the case id, what was missed, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (triage error, escalation delay, drafting delay, incomplete closure) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any confirmed late notification, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-late-notification threshold for reportable cases.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who tested none of the sampled cases sign the workpaper.
Report results and any late notifications to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Lock and reconcile the quarter-end data extract
actions: Extract policy liability, in-force and claims data as of quarter-end from the policy administration and reserving systems.
Extract asset and investment data as of the same date from BlackRock Aladdin and the general ledger.
Reconcile the extracted liability total to the general ledger reserve balance and the asset total to the GL investment balance, resolving any break before proceeding.
Lock the reconciled data set and timestamp the lock in the capital close calendar.
checklist.done: liability and asset data reconcile to the general ledger and the data set is locked and timestamped by day 10 of the close.

checklist.step: Roll forward actuarial and economic assumptions
actions: Pull the prior quarter's approved assumption set (mortality/morbidity, lapse, expense, interest rate curve) from the model governance repository.
Update the interest rate curve and any economic assumption to quarter-end market data.
Flag any non-economic assumption due for its scheduled annual review and route it to the Reserving Actuary for updated experience analysis.
Load the rolled-forward assumption set into the actuarial modeling platform and version it.
checklist.done: the assumption set is rolled forward, economic assumptions are current to quarter-end, and the version is loaded and logged.

checklist.step: Run the LICAT/MCT capital model
actions: Load the locked data set and the versioned assumption set into the model run configuration.
Execute the full run computing required capital components (insurance risk, market risk, credit risk, operational risk per the LICAT/MCT formula) and available capital.
Check the run completed without error messages and that output record counts match the input data set counts.
Save the run outputs, logs and configuration snapshot to the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the model run completes cleanly with reconciled record counts and outputs saved with a full configuration snapshot.

checklist.step: Compute the capital ratio and compare to targets
actions: Compute the Total and Core ratios (LICAT) or the MCT ratio from the model's available and required capital outputs.
Compare the computed ratios to OSFI's supervisory target and to the board-approved internal capital target.
Flag any ratio below the internal target as an immediate escalation, and any ratio below the supervisory target as a critical escalation.
Record the computed ratios and their movement from the prior quarter on the results summary.
checklist.done: the capital ratios are computed, compared to both target levels, and any shortfall is flagged for escalation.

checklist.step: Perform variance analysis against the prior quarter
actions: Decompose the ratio movement into assumption changes, in-force movement, market movement and new business/capital actions.
Compare the decomposition to the expected drivers identified during planning; investigate any unexplained variance beyond a defined materiality threshold.
Document the investigation outcome for any material unexplained variance.
Attach the variance analysis to the results summary.
checklist.done: the ratio movement is decomposed and every material unexplained variance has a documented investigation outcome.

checklist.step: Review results with the Appointed Actuary
actions: Review the model run configuration, ratio computation and variance analysis for reasonableness against the entity's risk profile.
Confirm the assumption roll-forward and any annual assumption update were performed per the documented governance process.
Raise any concern back to the Capital Model Actuary for rework before sign-off.
Sign the results summary confirming actuarial reasonableness.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary has reviewed and signed the results summary, with any concerns resolved before sign-off.

checklist.step: Obtain Model Risk validation of the quarter's run
actions: Confirm the model version used matches the currently validated version on the model inventory.
Spot-check a sample of model inputs and outputs against the locked data set and the assumption version.
Confirm any model change since the last validation went through the change control process.
Log the validation check outcome on the model governance repository record.
checklist.done: the run is confirmed on a validated model version with change control evidence, and the check is logged.

checklist.step: Prepare the OSFI capital return
actions: Map the model outputs and computed ratios onto OSFI's prescribed capital return template line by line.
Cross-check every mapped figure against the results summary and the general ledger reconciliation.
Complete the return's supporting schedules (risk component breakdown, available capital composition).
Route the completed return to the Capital Management Manager for review.
checklist.done: the capital return is fully populated, cross-checked to source, and routed for review.

checklist.step: Review and approve the capital return before submission
actions: Compare every return line to the Appointed-Actuary-signed results summary for consistency.
Confirm no unresolved data reconciliation break or model validation concern remains open.
Approve the return for CFO sign-off, or send it back with specific correction items.
Record the approval and any correction cycle on the return's workpaper.
checklist.done: the return is confirmed consistent with the signed results and approved, with any correction cycle documented.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO sign-off and submit the return to OSFI
actions: Review the approved capital return and the ratio comparison against internal and supervisory targets.
Sign the return as CFO attestation.
Submit the return through the institution's OSFI regulatory filing channel within the required deadline.
Log the submission timestamp and confirmation reference on the workpaper.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed and the return is submitted to OSFI with a logged confirmation reference.

checklist.step: Escalate any ratio shortfall against internal or supervisory targets
actions: Where the computed ratio breaches the internal target, brief the Chief Financial Officer and the Board Risk Committee within five business days.
Where the ratio breaches the OSFI supervisory target, initiate the capital contingency/escalation plan immediately.
Present remediation options (capital injection, reinsurance, business mix change) with a recommended path and timeline.
Record the decision and remediation timeline against the quarter's capital file.
checklist.done: any target breach is briefed within five business days with a recorded, owned remediation timeline.

checklist.step: Log calculation exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every data reconciliation break, model run error, or missed close-calendar milestone in the quarter.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of the next quarter's close.
Track exceptions to closure with evidence of the fix.
Report the quarter's exception count to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: every calculation exception has a root-caused, owned tracker issue with a remediation date and tracked closure.

checklist.step: File the calculation evidence for the retention period
actions: Assemble the locked data set reference, assumption version, model run outputs/logs, results summary and sign-offs.
File the package in the model governance repository under the quarter and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the package is indexed and retrievable by quarter and legal entity.
Notify the Capital Management Manager that the quarter's file is closed.
checklist.done: the quarter's calculation package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by quarter and entity.

checklist.step: Report the quarter's capital position to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Summarize the computed ratios, movement from prior quarter and any target breach or exception for the board package.
Upload the summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the summary and record committee questions and direction in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the quarter's capital position and any breaches or exceptions.

checklist.step: Refresh the calculation procedure after any OSFI guideline update
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to Guideline A-4 or the LICAT/MCT formula.
Assess the impact of any change on the calculation methodology and the close-calendar timeline.
Update the documented procedure and brief the Capital Model Actuary and Capital Management Manager on the change.
Record the procedure version update and its effective quarter.
checklist.done: the calculation procedure is current against the latest OSFI guideline, with the update briefed and recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of capital calculation runs for the test period
actions: List every quarterly and annual capital calculation run performed in the test period, by legal entity.
Reconcile the run list to the model governance repository's logged run history and resolve any count difference before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population as complete.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the model governance repository's run log and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take the annual run for every legal entity plus any quarter where the ratio breached the internal target.
Take a random, seeded sample of at least two additional quarterly runs per entity.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every annual run and every target-breach quarter.

testing.step: Reconcile the sampled run's input data to source systems
actions: Independently re-pull the liability and asset balances from the general ledger and BlackRock Aladdin for the sampled quarter-end.
Compare the re-pulled balances to the locked data set used in the sampled run.
Flag any discrepancy beyond a defined immaterial tolerance as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled run's input data is independently reconciled to source, or a discrepancy is logged.

testing.step: Independently re-perform the capital ratio computation
actions: Re-run the model using the same locked data and assumption version in a segregated test environment.
Independently compute the Total/Core or MCT ratio from the re-run outputs.
Compare the re-performed ratio to the reported ratio; any difference beyond 1 percentage point is an exception.
Capture the re-performance log into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled run's ratio is independently re-performed and reconciled within tolerance, or an exception logged.

testing.step: Verify the assumption set used matches the approved governance version
actions: Pull the assumption version used in the sampled run from the model governance repository.
Confirm it matches the version approved through the assumption governance process, with no unapproved manual override.
Flag any unapproved or undocumented assumption change as an exception.
testing.done: the assumption version used is confirmed approved and unmodified, or an unapproved change is logged.

testing.step: Test the model validation status for each sampled run
actions: Confirm the model version used in the sampled run was validated and on the current model inventory at the time of the run.
Check any model change between validation and the run date went through change control.
Flag any run performed on an unvalidated or uncontrolled model version as a control exception.
testing.done: every sampled run's model version is confirmed validated and change-controlled, or a control exception is logged.

testing.step: Trace the sampled ratios to the filed OSFI capital return
actions: Pull the submitted OSFI capital return for the sampled period and compare every mapped figure to the results summary and re-performed computation.
Confirm the CFO sign-off date pre-dates the OSFI submission timestamp.
Flag any mapping error or missing sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: the filed return traces to the sampled results with a pre-dated sign-off, or discrepancies are logged.

testing.step: Verify escalation occurred for any target breach in the sample
actions: For any sampled quarter with a ratio below the internal or supervisory target, confirm the five-business-day CRO briefing occurred with a timestamp.
Confirm a remediation timeline is recorded and was subsequently tracked to completion or a later status update.
Flag any missing or late escalation as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled target breach shows a timely escalation and a tracked remediation timeline, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per testing exception with the run id, what was missed, and the reporting impact.
Assign a root cause (data break, model error, unapproved assumption, escalation delay) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the 1-percentage-point tolerance and zero-unapproved-assumption threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who performed no part of the sampled re-computation sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Calibrate the internal capital target for the annual cycle
actions: Pull the current ORSA risk profile assessment and the prior year's internal target from the model governance repository.
Recompute the recommended internal target margin above the OSFI supervisory target, reflecting the risk profile, business plan growth and stress test results.
Route the recommended target to the Chief Risk Officer for concurrence before board submission.
Prepare the board paper setting out the recommended target and its rationale.
checklist.done: a recommended internal target with documented rationale is concurred by the CRO and ready for board approval.

checklist.step: Obtain Board Risk Committee approval of the internal target
actions: Upload the target-setting board paper to the board portal ahead of the scheduled meeting.
Present the recommended target, its margin above the supervisory target, and the ORSA linkage.
Record the approved target and any board-directed adjustment in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal as the year's target authority.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has approved and minuted the internal capital target for the cycle.

checklist.step: Configure the monitoring dashboard with the approved target and buffers
actions: Enter the board-approved internal target and OSFI's supervisory target as reference lines on the capital ratio dashboard.
Set an early-warning buffer (e.g. 10 percentage points above the internal target) that triggers a same-day alert when breached.
Connect the dashboard's data feed to the latest quarterly model output plus the intra-quarter capital-impact estimate feed.
Test the alert by simulating a ratio value inside the buffer zone and confirming the Capital Management Manager receives the alert.
checklist.done: the dashboard shows both target lines, the buffer alert is configured, and a simulated breach confirms the alert fires.

checklist.step: Refresh the intra-quarter capital-impact estimate on the configured cadence
actions: Pull the latest in-force movement, market movement and known capital actions (dividends, reinsurance, capital raises) since the last quarterly run.
Apply the sensitivities from the last full model run to estimate the current ratio position between quarterly closes.
Load the estimate into the BI/reporting platform dashboard on the configured weekly/monthly cadence.
Flag any refresh that could not be completed on schedule to the Capital Management Manager the same day.
checklist.done: the intra-quarter estimate is refreshed on the configured cadence with any missed refresh flagged the same day.

checklist.step: Monitor the dashboard for buffer or target proximity
actions: Review the dashboard at each refresh and confirm the estimated ratio position against both target lines.
Where the estimate falls inside the early-warning buffer, open an escalation case the same business day.
Where the estimate approaches the OSFI supervisory target, treat it as a critical escalation regardless of buffer status.
Log the review outcome even when no breach occurs, to evidence continuous monitoring.
checklist.done: every refresh is reviewed and logged, with same-day escalation opened for any buffer or supervisory-target proximity.

checklist.step: Escalate a buffer breach to the CFO and Chief Risk Officer
actions: Brief the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Risk Officer the same business day the buffer is breached, with the estimate, the driver of the movement and any pending capital actions.
Request direction on whether an out-of-cycle full model run is warranted to confirm the estimate.
Record the briefing timestamp and the direction given on the escalation case.
checklist.done: the CFO and CRO are briefed the same business day of a buffer breach, with a recorded direction on next steps.

checklist.step: Confirm the estimate with an out-of-cycle model run where warranted
actions: Run the full capital model with current data where the CFO/CRO direct confirmation of a buffer or target breach.
Compare the confirmed ratio to the intra-quarter estimate and note any material difference for the estimation methodology's future calibration.
Update the escalation case with the confirmed ratio.
File the out-of-cycle run in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: the out-of-cycle run confirms or corrects the estimate, and the result is filed and reflected on the escalation case.

checklist.step: Activate the capital contingency plan on a supervisory-target proximity or breach
actions: Where the confirmed ratio is at or below the OSFI supervisory target (or the board-set critical threshold), activate the capital contingency plan.
Convene the capital contingency working group (CFO, CRO, Appointed Actuary, Treasury Manager) within two business days.
Select and sequence remediation options: capital injection, reinsurance, dividend suspension, or business mix change.
Brief OSFI proactively per the institution's supervisory relationship protocol rather than waiting for the next scheduled filing.
checklist.done: the contingency plan is activated, the working group convened within two business days, and OSFI proactively briefed.

checklist.step: Report the escalation and remediation plan to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Prepare a board paper covering the breach, its driver, the confirmed ratio, and the selected remediation options with timeline.
Upload the paper to the board portal ahead of an out-of-cycle or the next scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the paper and record the committee's direction and any approval needed for the remediation actions in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the breach and the remediation plan, with any needed approvals recorded.

checklist.step: Execute and track the remediation actions to closure
actions: Execute the approved remediation action (capital raise, reinsurance placement, dividend suspension) per the board-approved plan.
Update the dashboard estimate as each remediation action's capital impact is realized.
Confirm the ratio has returned above the internal target buffer before declaring the escalation closed.
Log the closure date and the confirming ratio on the escalation case.
checklist.done: remediation actions are executed, the dashboard reflects their impact, and closure is confirmed only once the ratio clears the buffer.

checklist.step: Log monitoring exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any missed refresh cycle, un-escalated buffer breach, or dashboard configuration error found in the period.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Report the period's exception count to the Chief Financial Officer.
Track exceptions to closure with evidence of the fix.
checklist.done: every monitoring exception has a root-caused, owned tracker issue with a remediation date and tracked closure.

checklist.step: Review and re-approve the escalation triggers annually
actions: Review the buffer trigger level and escalation timelines against the past year's actual ratio volatility and any near-miss events.
Recommend an adjustment to the buffer or escalation timeline where the past year's experience warrants it.
Route the recommendation through the same annual target-setting board approval as the internal target itself.
Record the reviewed and (where changed) re-approved triggers in the procedure document.
checklist.done: the escalation triggers are reviewed annually against actual experience and re-approved through the board process.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring and escalation evidence for the retention period
actions: Export dashboard snapshots, escalation case records and board reporting for the period.
File the export into the compliance evidence repository and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by quarter and by escalation case id.
Notify the CFO that the period's monitoring evidence is filed.
checklist.done: monitoring and escalation evidence is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by quarter and case id.

checklist.step: Confirm the monitoring procedure reflects the current OSFI A-4 guideline
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to Guideline A-4's supervisory target or intervention staging.
Assess the impact of any change on the internal target margin and the escalation trigger design.
Update the documented procedure and brief the Board Risk Committee of any material change.
Record the procedure version update and its effective date.
checklist.done: the monitoring procedure is current against the latest A-4 guideline, with material changes briefed to the board.

checklist.step: Report the quarterly monitoring summary to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Summarize the quarter's refresh cadence adherence, buffer proximity events and any escalations for the board package.
Upload the summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the summary and record committee questions and direction in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the quarter's capital monitoring summary.

testing.step: Build the population of monitoring refreshes and escalation events for the quarter
actions: Extract the dashboard's refresh log for the quarter, listing every scheduled and completed refresh date.
Extract every escalation case opened in the quarter from the escalation tracker.
Reconcile the refresh log to the configured cadence and flag any gap before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population as complete.
testing.done: the refresh and escalation population is reconciled to the configured cadence and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of escalation events (buffer breaches and supervisory-target proximities).
Take a random, seeded sample of at least 25% of routine refreshes, minimum 10 refreshes.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of escalation events.

testing.step: Recompute the intra-quarter estimate for sampled refreshes
actions: Pull the source in-force, market movement and capital-action data used for each sampled refresh.
Independently reapply the sensitivity methodology to recompute the estimated ratio.
Compare the recomputed estimate to the dashboard's recorded value; flag any difference beyond a defined tolerance.
testing.done: every sampled refresh's estimate is independently recomputed and reconciled within tolerance, or an exception logged.

testing.step: Verify same-day escalation timing for sampled breach events
actions: For each sampled escalation event, compare the dashboard alert timestamp to the CFO/CRO briefing timestamp on the escalation case.
Confirm the briefing occurred the same business day as the alert.
Flag any escalation briefed later than the same business day as a control exception.
testing.done: every sampled escalation event shows same-business-day briefing, or a timing exception is logged.

testing.step: Trace out-of-cycle confirmation runs to the model governance repository
actions: For each sampled escalation event that triggered an out-of-cycle model run, confirm the run exists in the model governance repository.
Compare the confirmed ratio in the run output to the ratio recorded on the escalation case.
Flag any escalation event lacking a confirming run where one was directed.
testing.done: every directed out-of-cycle run is traced to a filed model output matching the escalation case, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify contingency plan activation and board reporting for critical events
actions: For any sampled event at or below the supervisory target or board-set critical threshold, confirm the contingency working group convened within two business days.
Confirm the board paper and minutes exist in the board portal recording the remediation plan and any approvals.
Flag any critical event missing timely contingency activation or board reporting.
testing.done: every critical sampled event shows timely contingency activation and board reporting, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Confirm remediation actions were executed and closure was evidence-based
actions: For each closed escalation case in the sample, confirm the remediation action recorded actually occurred (capital raise confirmation, reinsurance treaty execution, dividend suspension record).
Confirm the closing ratio recorded on the case is supported by a dashboard snapshot or model run showing the ratio above the buffer.
Flag any case closed without supporting evidence as a false-closure exception.
testing.done: every sampled closed case has evidenced remediation and an evidenced closing ratio, or a false-closure exception is logged.

testing.step: Check refresh-cadence adherence for the sampled routine refreshes
actions: Compare each sampled refresh's actual completion date to its scheduled date per the configured cadence.
Flag any refresh missed and not caught by the same-day flag-to-Capital-Management-Manager control.
Confirm any flagged missed refresh has a corresponding tracker exception.
testing.done: refresh-cadence adherence is confirmed for the sample, with unflagged misses logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per testing exception with the refresh/escalation id, what was missed, and the monitoring impact.
Assign a root cause (data feed gap, calculation error, escalation delay, false closure) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-late-escalation threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer outside the Capital Management team sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.
