checklist.step: Build and publish the annual OSFI filing calendar
actions: List every return due in the coming fiscal year: quarterly capital returns, the ORSA Key Metrics Report, the Appointed Actuary's Report, and any other OSFI prescribed return for each legal entity.
Compute each return's due date from OSFI's published filing deadlines and the entity's fiscal year-end.
Enter each return, its due date, preparer and reviewer into the Internal Regulatory System filing calendar.
Circulate the published calendar to all named preparers and reviewers.
checklist.done: the filing calendar is published with every due return, its due date, preparer and reviewer assigned.

checklist.step: Prepare each return from its source data
actions: Pull the finalized results package for the return period from the actuarial modeling platform (capital returns) or the ORSA report and risk register (ORSA KMR).
Map each source figure onto the OSFI-prescribed return template, line by line.
Cross-check every mapped figure against the finalized results package and the general ledger where applicable.
Save the drafted return under the filing calendar's return record with a version number.
checklist.done: each return is drafted, fully mapped and cross-checked to source, versioned and attached to its calendar record.

checklist.step: Route the draft return through internal technical review
actions: Assign the draft to the named technical reviewer (Capital Model Actuary for capital returns, Enterprise Risk Manager for ORSA KMR).
Reviewer checks every line against the source results package and flags any mapping or computation error.
Route flagged items back to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst for correction and re-submission.
Confirm the reviewer's sign-off is recorded on the return record before escalating for executive sign-off.
checklist.done: the draft return carries a recorded technical reviewer sign-off with no open flagged items.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary sign-off on actuarially derived returns
actions: Review the ORSA Key Metrics Report and Appointed Actuary's Report for actuarial reasonableness against the underlying valuation and capital work.
Confirm the required actuarial opinion or certification language is present and unmodified from the approved template wording.
Sign the actuarial certification page.
Return any concern to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst for correction before re-presenting for sign-off.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary has signed the actuarial certification with no open concern.

checklist.step: Obtain executive sign-off before submission
actions: Review the fully reviewed and (where applicable) actuarially certified return.
Confirm the return reconciles to the results package the Board Risk Committee already saw, with no unexplained late change.
Sign the executive attestation on the return.
Authorize the Regulatory Reporting Manager to submit.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed the executive attestation and authorized submission.

checklist.step: Submit the return to OSFI ahead of the due date
actions: Submit the signed return through the institution's designated OSFI regulatory return filing channel.
Record the submission timestamp on the filing calendar record.
Confirm the submission is on or before the due date; if not, immediately open a late-filing exception.
Retain the submission confirmation receipt against the return record.
checklist.done: the return is submitted with a logged, on-or-before-due-date timestamp and a retained confirmation receipt.

checklist.step: Track and log the OSFI acknowledgement
actions: Monitor for OSFI's acknowledgement or any follow-up query on the submitted return.
Log the acknowledgement date against the filing calendar record.
Route any OSFI follow-up query to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the relevant technical reviewer within one business day.
Close the calendar record only once acknowledgement is received or the follow-up query is resolved.
checklist.done: the acknowledgement (or resolved follow-up query) is logged and the calendar record is closed accordingly.

checklist.step: Escalate any return approaching its due date without sign-off
actions: Review the filing calendar's T-5-day escalation list each week.
For any return not yet fully signed off inside T-5 days, convene the preparer and reviewer to close the gap immediately.
Where the due date genuinely cannot be met, prepare a proactive late-filing notification to OSFI rather than allowing a silent miss.
Record the escalation and its resolution on the return record.
checklist.done: no return reaches its due date without either full sign-off or a documented, proactive late-filing notification.

checklist.step: Investigate and remediate any late or restated filing
actions: Open a tracker issue for any return filed after its due date or subsequently restated.
Assign a root cause (source data delay, reviewer bandwidth, template change missed) and an owner for the process fix.
Set a remediation date for the process fix and confirm it is in place before the next filing cycle for that return type.
Brief the Chief Financial Officer on the root cause and fix.
checklist.done: every late or restated filing has a root-caused tracker issue, an owner, and a confirmed process fix before the next cycle.

checklist.step: Reconcile the annual filing calendar to actual submissions
actions: At fiscal year-end, compare the published filing calendar to the actual submission log for every return due in the year.
Confirm every planned return was in fact submitted, with no return silently dropped from the calendar.
Investigate and log as an exception any return on the calendar with no corresponding submission record.
Carry forward the confirmed submission history into the next year's calendar build.
checklist.done: the calendar reconciles 100% to actual submissions, with any silently missed return logged as an exception.

checklist.step: File the return evidence for the retention period
actions: Assemble the final return, all sign-offs, the submission confirmation and the OSFI acknowledgement.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the return type and period, applying the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by return type, entity and period.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager that the period's evidence is filed.
checklist.done: each return's evidence package is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by type, entity and period.

checklist.step: Monitor OSFI for return template or deadline changes
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to the capital return, ORSA KMR or AAR templates and their filing deadlines.
Assess the impact of any change on the preparation procedure and the filing calendar.
Update the documented procedure and the filing calendar, and brief all preparers and reviewers of the change.
Record the procedure version update and its effective filing cycle.
checklist.done: the filing procedure and calendar are current against the latest OSFI templates and deadlines, with preparers briefed.

checklist.step: Report the year's filing performance to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Summarize the year's on-time filing rate, any late filings or restatements, and their remediation status for the board package.
Upload the summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the summary and record committee questions and direction in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed and minuted the year's OSFI filing performance.

checklist.step: Respond to any OSFI inquiry on a filed return
actions: Log the inquiry's receipt date and content on the return record and start the internal response clock.
Route the technical question to the relevant preparer/reviewer and route any legal question to General Counsel.
Route the drafted response through the same executive sign-off chain as the original return before sending.
Log the response submission date and file the correspondence with the return's evidence package.
checklist.done: every OSFI inquiry is logged, routed, signed off and responded to, with the correspondence filed against the return.

checklist.step: Reconcile the year's submitted returns to the audited financial statements
actions: After year-end audit sign-off, pull the audited financial statement balances for reserves, capital and investments.
Compare those balances to the figures used in the year's capital returns and the ORSA Key Metrics Report.
Investigate and document any difference beyond a defined immaterial threshold, noting whether it requires a return restatement.
File the reconciliation against the year's filing evidence package.
checklist.done: every submitted return for the year is reconciled to the audited financial statements with differences documented.

testing.step: Build the population of returns due in the test period
actions: Extract the full filing calendar for the test period, listing every capital, ORSA KMR and AAR return due by entity.
Reconcile the extract to OSFI's published filing deadline schedule for the relevant fiscal year-ends.
Sign the reconciled population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to OSFI's published deadlines and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of annual returns (ORSA KMR, AAR) and any return previously flagged late or restated.
Take a random, seeded sample of at least 50% of quarterly capital returns.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of annual returns and prior exceptions.

testing.step: Verify timeliness of each sampled submission
actions: Compare the logged submission timestamp to the return's computed due date for each sampled return.
Flag any submission after the due date as an exception, regardless of whether OSFI raised the lateness.
Capture the submission confirmation receipt into the workpaper as evidence.
testing.done: every sampled return's timeliness is verified against its due date, with late submissions logged.

testing.step: Trace each sampled return's figures to the underlying results package
actions: Compare every mapped line on the sampled return to the finalized results package (model output or ORSA report) used to prepare it.
Flag any mapping discrepancy or figure that does not tie to source.
Confirm the technical reviewer's sign-off pre-dates the submission timestamp.
testing.done: every sampled return's figures are traced to source with a pre-dated technical review sign-off, or discrepancies logged.

testing.step: Confirm executive and actuarial sign-off completeness
actions: Confirm the CFO executive attestation is present and dated before the submission timestamp for every sampled return.
For ORSA KMR and AAR, confirm the Appointed Actuary's certification is present, dated, and uses the approved certification wording.
Flag any missing, undated or non-conforming sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled return shows complete, pre-dated, and (where applicable) conforming executive and actuarial sign-off, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Confirm OSFI acknowledgement was received and logged
actions: Confirm an acknowledgement record exists for each sampled submission.
Where a follow-up query was raised, confirm it was routed and resolved within a reasonable timeframe with correspondence on file.
Flag any sampled return with no acknowledgement record or an unresolved follow-up query.
testing.done: acknowledgement or resolved follow-up is confirmed for every sampled return, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the full-year calendar to actual submissions
actions: Independently compare the full-year filing calendar to the submission log, not just the sample.
Confirm no return was silently dropped from the calendar without a submission record.
Flag any calendar-to-submission gap as a population-completeness exception.
testing.done: the full-year calendar is confirmed reconciled to actual submissions, or completeness gaps are logged.

testing.step: Test remediation of any prior-period late or restated filing
actions: Pull every tracker issue for a late or restated filing from the prior period.
Confirm the recorded process fix is genuinely in place (e.g. an earlier internal deadline, an added reviewer) for the current period's equivalent return.
Flag any repeat late filing of the same return type as a control-failure exception, not a routine finding.
testing.done: prior-period remediation is confirmed operating, or a repeat late filing is logged as a control failure.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per testing exception with the return, what was missed, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (source delay, reviewer bandwidth, mapping error, missed calendar entry) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the exception rate and compare both to the zero-late-annual-return threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who prepared or reviewed none of the sampled returns sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Add or re-tier any new material risk, and retire any risk no longer applicable with a documented rationale.
Publish the confirmed risk universe as the basis for this cycle's ORSA.
checklist.done: the risk universe is refreshed, cross-functionally consulted, and published with documented additions/retirements.

checklist.step: Score each risk for materiality and assess reasonably foreseeable severity
actions: Score each risk on likelihood and impact using the board-approved risk appetite scale.
Identify reasonably foreseeable severe-but-plausible scenarios for each material risk, drawing on the stress-testing scenario set.
Route the scoring and scenario identification to the risk category owner for validation.
Compile the validated materiality assessment into the ORSA workpaper.
checklist.done: every risk has a validated materiality score and, for material risks, an identified severe-but-plausible scenario.

checklist.step: Link the risk assessment to the current stress/scenario test results
actions: Pull the current cycle's stress and scenario test outputs from the actuarial modeling platform.
Map each material risk on the universe to the stress test scenario(s) that quantify its capital impact.
Flag any material risk without a corresponding quantified scenario and route it to Risk/Actuarial for a new scenario design.
Attach the mapped scenario results to the ORSA workpaper.
checklist.done: every material risk maps to a quantified stress/scenario test result, with gaps routed for new scenario design.

checklist.step: Assess capital needs against internal targets using the linked results
actions: Aggregate the capital impact of the mapped scenarios to derive the forward-looking capital needs assessment.
Compare the assessed capital needs to the current board-approved internal capital target and the OSFI supervisory target.
Document any identified gap between assessed needs and the current target, with a recommendation to adjust the target or hold additional capital.
Route the capital needs assessment to the Chief Financial Officer for review.
checklist.done: a capital needs assessment derived from the linked scenarios is compared to internal/supervisory targets with any gap documented.

checklist.step: Congruence-check the ORSA against the business and strategic plan
actions: Compare the ORSA's risk universe and capital needs assessment to the current business plan's growth assumptions and strategic initiatives.
Flag any strategic initiative (new product line, market expansion, major acquisition) not yet reflected in the risk universe or capital needs assessment.
Route flagged gaps to the Enterprise Risk Manager for inclusion before the report is drafted.
Record the congruence check outcome in the ORSA workpaper.
checklist.done: the ORSA is confirmed congruent with the current business/strategic plan, with any gap routed for inclusion before drafting.

checklist.step: Draft the ORSA report
actions: Draft the report covering: risk universe and materiality assessment, scenario/stress test linkage, capital needs assessment, target comparison, and the strategic-plan congruence check.
State key assumptions explicitly, including the assumptions underlying each linked scenario.
Draw a conclusion on whether current and projected capital is adequate for the assessed risk profile over the planning horizon.
Save the drafted report in the GRC platform's ORSA workflow for review.
checklist.done: a complete draft report covering risk universe, scenario linkage, capital needs and a stated adequacy conclusion is saved for review.

checklist.step: Route the draft through senior management review
actions: Review the draft for completeness against the risk universe and for consistency with the linked scenario results.
Convene senior management (CFO, Chief Actuary, CUO, CISO) to review and challenge the conclusion.
Route any required correction back to the Enterprise Risk Manager and confirm rework before re-presenting.
Sign the senior management review record.
checklist.done: senior management has reviewed and challenged the draft, corrections are resolved, and the CRO has signed the review record.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary input on the actuarial elements
actions: Review the scenario linkage and capital needs assessment for actuarial reasonableness.
Confirm the stress test assumptions used are consistent with the current valuation and capital model assumption governance.
Provide written comments or concurrence on the report's actuarial content.
Attach the Appointed Actuary's comments to the report record.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary has reviewed the actuarial content and provided written comments or concurrence.

checklist.step: Present the ORSA report to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the senior-management-reviewed report to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present the risk universe, scenario linkage, capital needs assessment and conclusion, taking committee questions.
Record the committee's acceptance, any requested revision, or any additional scenario request in the minutes.
Where a revision is requested, route it back to the Enterprise Risk Manager and re-present before final sign-off.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has reviewed the report and recorded acceptance or requested revisions in the minutes.

checklist.step: Obtain final Board Risk Committee sign-off
actions: Confirm any board-requested revision has been incorporated and re-presented.
Record the board's formal sign-off date and signatory on the final report.
File the signed report as the year's approved ORSA in the board portal.
Notify the Enterprise Risk Manager that the report is board-approved and ready for the ORSA Key Metrics Report submission.
checklist.done: the final ORSA report carries a recorded board sign-off date and is filed as approved.

checklist.step: Prepare and submit the ORSA Key Metrics Report to OSFI
actions: Map the board-approved ORSA's internal targets and key risk/capital metrics onto OSFI's prescribed ORSA Key Metrics Report template (life or P&C form).
Cross-check every mapped figure against the signed ORSA report and the latest capital calculation.
Route the completed KMR through the Regulatory Reporting Manager and CFO sign-off chain.
Submit the KMR to OSFI within the annual deadline and log the submission timestamp.
checklist.done: the ORSA Key Metrics Report is mapped, cross-checked, signed off and submitted to OSFI with a logged timestamp.

checklist.step: Log ORSA cycle exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any risk universe gap, missing scenario linkage, or late board review identified during the cycle.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of the next cycle.
Report the cycle's exception count to the Chief Risk Officer.
Track exceptions to closure with evidence of the fix.
checklist.done: every ORSA cycle exception has a root-caused, owned tracker issue with a remediation date and tracked closure.

checklist.step: Re-run the ORSA on any material change to the risk profile
actions: Monitor for triggers requiring an off-cycle ORSA update: major acquisition, new product line, material adverse event, or significant market shift.
Assess whether the trigger materially changes the risk universe or capital needs assessment.
Where material, initiate an off-cycle ORSA refresh through the same review and board sign-off chain as the annual cycle.
Record the trigger assessment and the decision to refresh or not in the ORSA workpaper.
checklist.done: every potential trigger is assessed and, where material, an off-cycle ORSA refresh is initiated through full sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain the ORSA evidence for the retention period
actions: Assemble the risk universe assessment, scenario linkage workpapers, senior management and actuarial review records, the signed report and board minutes.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the cycle year and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by cycle year and legal entity.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer that the cycle evidence is filed.
checklist.done: the cycle's ORSA evidence package is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by year and entity.

checklist.step: Refresh the ORSA procedure after any OSFI guideline update
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to Guideline E-19 or the ORSA Key Metrics Report template.
Assess the impact of any change on the ORSA cycle procedure and timeline.
Update the documented procedure and brief the Enterprise Risk Manager and Appointed Actuary on the change.
Record the procedure version update and its effective cycle.
checklist.done: the ORSA procedure is current against the latest OSFI guideline, with the update briefed and recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of risk universe entries and linked scenarios for the cycle
actions: Extract the full published risk universe for the cycle from the GRC platform.
Extract the scenario linkage mapping and the capital needs assessment workpaper.
Reconcile the risk universe to the prior cycle's list plus documented additions/retirements before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population as complete.
testing.done: the risk universe and scenario linkage population is reconciled and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of risks scored material/high on the current universe.
Take a random, seeded sample of at least 25% of lower-scored risks, minimum 10 risks.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of material/high-scored risks.

testing.step: Test risk universe completeness against independent sources
actions: Compare the published risk universe to the current internal audit findings register, incident log and external risk intelligence (industry loss events, regulatory bulletins).
Identify any material risk evident in those sources but absent from the ORSA risk universe.
Flag any omission as a completeness exception, not a documentation note.
testing.done: the risk universe is independently cross-checked for completeness, with any material omission logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality scoring for sampled risks
actions: Independently score each sampled risk on likelihood and impact using the same board-approved appetite scale, without viewing the recorded score first.
Compare the independent score to the recorded score; any material difference is an exception.
Capture the independent scoring worksheet into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled risk's materiality score is independently re-performed and reconciled, or an exception logged.

testing.step: Verify the scenario linkage and re-trace the capital impact
actions: For each sampled material risk, confirm the linked stress/scenario test genuinely quantifies that risk's capital impact, not a loosely related scenario.
Trace the scenario's capital impact figure to the actuarial modeling platform's run output.
Flag any weak or missing linkage, or any figure that does not tie to the model output, as an exception.
testing.done: scenario linkage and capital impact figures are verified and traced to source for every sampled material risk, or exceptions logged.

testing.step: Recompute the capital needs assessment against internal/supervisory targets
actions: Independently aggregate the sampled scenarios' capital impacts to recompute the forward-looking capital needs figure.
Compare the recomputed figure to the reported capital needs assessment and to the internal/supervisory targets.
Flag any material discrepancy or any undocumented gap between assessed needs and current targets.
testing.done: the capital needs assessment is independently recomputed and reconciled, with gaps against targets confirmed documented or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm strategic-plan congruence was genuinely assessed
actions: Compare the current business/strategic plan's major initiatives to the ORSA's congruence-check record.
Confirm every major initiative identified in the plan is reflected in the risk universe or capital needs assessment.
Flag any initiative present in the plan but absent from the ORSA as a congruence exception.
testing.done: strategic-plan congruence is independently verified against the current plan, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Verify board sign-off timing and completeness
actions: Confirm the board portal record shows the ORSA report presented and sign-off recorded within the annual cycle window.
Confirm any board-requested revision was incorporated and re-presented before the final sign-off date.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's written comments are attached and pre-date the board sign-off.
Flag any late, missing, or unincorporated-revision sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: board sign-off timing, revision incorporation and Appointed Actuary comments are verified, or exceptions logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per testing exception with the risk/scenario/report element, what was missed, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (universe gap, weak scenario linkage, congruence gap, sign-off delay) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-material-risk-omission threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who contributed to no part of the sampled ORSA content sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Design the DCAT base and adverse scenario set for the cycle
actions: Draw the base scenario from the current business plan and the adverse scenarios from severe-but-plausible risk events on the ORSA risk universe (mortality/morbidity shock, interest rate shock, lapse spike, credit downgrade, climate physical/transition scenario).
Confirm at least one adverse scenario combines two or more risk factors to test correlated stress, not single-factor shocks only.
Route the draft scenario set to the Chief Actuary and Chief Risk Officer for sign-off before scheduling model runs.
Record the approved scenario set and its rationale in the DCAT workpaper.
checklist.done: an approved base and multi-factor adverse scenario set is signed off by the Chief Actuary and CRO before runs are scheduled.

checklist.step: Execute the DCAT model runs
actions: Load the approved scenario set and current assumption version into the actuarial modeling platform.
Execute each scenario projecting the capital ratio (LICAT/MCT) over the planning horizon under base and adverse conditions.
Confirm each run completes without error and produces a full projection period with no gap year.
Save the run outputs, logs and configuration snapshot to the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every approved scenario runs to completion with a full projection period, and outputs are saved with a configuration snapshot.

checklist.step: Identify the point of capital breach under each adverse scenario
actions: For each adverse scenario, identify the projection year (if any) where the ratio breaches the internal target, then the supervisory target.
Where no breach occurs within the planning horizon, confirm the margin held at the horizon's end.
Document management actions that would plausibly be taken before a breach (e.g. reinsurance, dividend suspension) and re-run with those actions applied as a secondary case.
Attach the breach analysis to the DCAT workpaper.
checklist.done: every adverse scenario has a documented breach point (or confirmed margin) and a management-action secondary case.

checklist.step: Review DCAT results with the Chief Risk Officer and CFO
actions: Review the breach analysis and management-action cases for plausibility and for consistency with the ORSA risk universe.
Confirm the CFO concurs the management actions modelled are realistically executable in the timeframe assumed.
Route any concern back to the Capital Model Actuary for scenario or assumption rework.
Sign the DCAT results review record.
checklist.done: the CRO and CFO have reviewed and signed the DCAT results, with any concern resolved before sign-off.

checklist.step: Feed the DCAT results into the ORSA and capital plan
actions: Attach the signed DCAT breach analysis to the current ORSA cycle's scenario linkage section.
Confirm the capital plan reflects any management action identified as necessary under the adverse scenarios.
Flag any DCAT finding that changes the ORSA's capital needs conclusion and route it to the Enterprise Risk Manager owning the ORSA report.
Record the DCAT-to-ORSA linkage in the ORSA workpaper.
checklist.done: the DCAT breach analysis is linked into the ORSA scenario section and any capital-plan impact is reflected.

checklist.step: Finalize and board-report the DCAT within the 180-day window
actions: Compile the final DCAT report covering scenario design, results, breach analysis and management actions.
Upload the report to the board portal ahead of the Board Risk Committee meeting, ensuring it lands inside 180 days of fiscal year-end.
Present the results and record the committee's acceptance or any additional scenario request in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal before the 180-day deadline.
checklist.done: the DCAT report is board-presented and minuted inside the 180-day window, with the minutes filed.

checklist.step: Distribute the annual fit-and-proper questionnaire
actions: Identify every director, senior manager and head of an oversight function in scope for the annual reconfirmation.
Distribute the fit-and-proper questionnaire (integrity, competence, financial soundness declarations) through the GRC platform to each individual.
Set a completion deadline and track outstanding responses in the GRC workflow.
Escalate any individual who has not responded within 15 days of the deadline to the Board Governance Lead.
checklist.done: the questionnaire is distributed to every in-scope individual with tracked completion and escalation for non-response.

checklist.step: Review completed questionnaires and refresh background checks
actions: Review each completed questionnaire for any disclosed change (new directorship, legal proceeding, financial difficulty, regulatory action).
Refresh the background/credit check for any individual with a disclosed change or where the prior check has aged past the policy refresh interval.
Compare refreshed check results to the individual's declaration and flag any discrepancy.
Log the review outcome and check refresh date against each individual's record.
checklist.done: every questionnaire is reviewed, background checks refreshed where triggered, and any discrepancy flagged and logged.

checklist.step: Assess and resolve any fit-and-proper concern
actions: For any flagged discrepancy or disclosed adverse item, assess its materiality to the individual's fitness for the role.
Where material, convene the Board Governance Committee to determine whether the individual remains fit and proper, with conditions if applicable.
Document the assessment, the decision and any conditions imposed.
Route confirmed unresolved concerns to the Corporate Secretary for OSFI notification assessment.
checklist.done: every flagged concern has a documented materiality assessment and a recorded fitness decision, with unresolved concerns routed for notification assessment.

checklist.step: Notify OSFI of any responsible-persons change or unresolved concern
actions: Determine whether the year's board/senior-management changes or an unresolved fit-and-proper concern triggers an OSFI responsible-persons notification under the ICA provisions.
Prepare the notification with the individual's role, the nature of the change or concern, and the institution's assessment.
Route the notification through General Counsel for review before submission.
Submit the notification to OSFI and log the submission date and any acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every triggering change or unresolved concern is notified to OSFI with a logged submission date and acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Compile the annual fit-and-proper attestation register
actions: Confirm every in-scope individual has a completed questionnaire, a current background check, and a recorded fitness decision.
Compile the attestation register showing status for every individual for the cycle.
Route the compiled register to the Board Governance Lead for final review.
File the signed-off register in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: a complete attestation register exists for every in-scope individual, reviewed and filed.

checklist.step: Report the fit-and-proper attestation outcomes to the Board Governance Committee
actions: Summarize the attestation register status, any flagged concern and its resolution, and any OSFI notification made in the cycle.
Upload the summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Board Governance Committee meeting.
Present the summary and record the committee's acknowledgement or any additional direction in the minutes.
Confirm the minutes are filed in the board portal alongside the DCAT board reporting record for the cycle.
checklist.done: the Board Governance Committee has reviewed and minuted the cycle's fit-and-proper attestation outcomes.

checklist.step: Log stress-testing and fit-and-proper exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any missed scenario run, missed 180-day deadline, or incomplete fit-and-proper item found in the cycle.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of the next cycle.
Report the cycle's exception count to the Board Risk Committee.
Track exceptions to closure with evidence of the fix.
checklist.done: every cycle exception has a root-caused, owned tracker issue with a remediation date and tracked closure.

checklist.step: Retain the stress-testing and fit-and-proper evidence for the retention period
actions: Assemble the DCAT scenario design, run outputs, breach analysis, board minutes, and the fit-and-proper attestation register.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under the cycle year and apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by cycle year and by individual name for fit-and-proper records.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer and Board Governance Lead that the cycle evidence is filed.
checklist.done: the cycle's stress-testing and fit-and-proper evidence is filed, retention-labelled and searchable.

checklist.step: Refresh the procedure after any OSFI corporate governance or E-19 update
actions: Monitor OSFI publications for updates to the Corporate Governance Guideline's fit-and-proper provisions or Guideline E-19's scenario testing expectations.
Assess the impact of any change on the questionnaire content, background check scope, or DCAT scenario design.
Update the documented procedure and brief the Corporate Secretary and Capital Model Actuary of the change.
Record the procedure version update and its effective cycle.
checklist.done: the procedure is current against the latest OSFI governance and E-19 guidance, with the update briefed and recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of stress scenarios and in-scope individuals for the cycle
actions: Extract the approved DCAT scenario list and the fit-and-proper in-scope individual list for the cycle.
Reconcile the individual list to the current board and senior management roster and resolve any count difference.
Sign the reconciled population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: both populations are reconciled to source rosters and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of DCAT adverse scenarios and 100% of directors and executive officers for the fit-and-proper population.
Take a random, seeded sample of at least 25% of remaining oversight-function heads.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of adverse scenarios and directors/executive officers.

testing.step: Re-perform the DCAT breach analysis for sampled scenarios
actions: Re-run each sampled adverse scenario in a segregated test environment using the same locked assumptions.
Independently identify the projection year of any capital target breach and compare to the reported breach analysis.
Flag any discrepancy in breach timing or magnitude as an exception.
Capture the re-performance log into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled scenario's breach analysis is independently re-performed and reconciled, or an exception logged.

testing.step: Recompute the 180-day timeline for the DCAT board report
actions: Pull the fiscal year-end date and the board portal timestamp of the DCAT report presentation.
Compute elapsed days and compare to the 180-day requirement.
Flag any cycle exceeding 180 days as an exception.
testing.done: the DCAT board reporting timeline is recomputed and confirmed within 180 days, or a breach is logged.

testing.step: Verify management actions modelled are realistically supportable
actions: For each sampled scenario's management-action case, confirm the action (reinsurance, dividend suspension, capital raise) has a documented feasibility basis, not just a modelling assumption.
Compare the assumed execution timeframe to precedent (prior actual execution times for similar actions) where available.
Flag any management action lacking a feasibility basis as an exception.
testing.done: management actions in the sampled scenarios are verified feasible and evidenced, or exceptions logged.

testing.step: Verify fit-and-proper questionnaire completion and background check currency
actions: Confirm each sampled individual's questionnaire is complete and signed within the cycle window.
Confirm the background check on file is within the policy refresh interval or was refreshed on a disclosed trigger.
Flag any missing, incomplete or stale questionnaire/check as an exception.
testing.done: questionnaire completion and background check currency are confirmed for every sampled individual, or exceptions logged.

testing.step: Test resolution of flagged fit-and-proper concerns
actions: Pull every sampled individual with a flagged discrepancy or disclosed adverse item.
Confirm a documented materiality assessment and fitness decision exists, and that any imposed condition was actually applied.
Confirm an OSFI notification was made where the assessment concluded one was required.
Flag any concern lacking a documented decision or a required notification as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled flagged concern shows a documented decision and any required OSFI notification, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Confirm the DCAT-to-ORSA linkage is genuinely reflected
actions: Compare the current ORSA report's scenario linkage section to the DCAT breach analysis for the sampled scenarios.
Confirm any capital-plan impact identified in the DCAT is reflected in the ORSA's capital needs conclusion.
Flag any inconsistency between the two documents as an exception.
testing.done: the DCAT-to-ORSA linkage is verified consistent for the sampled scenarios, or inconsistencies are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per testing exception with the scenario or individual, what was missed, and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (scenario design gap, timeline breach, incomplete attestation, unresolved concern) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any unresolved fit-and-proper concern, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-missed-180-day-deadline and zero-unresolved-fit-and-proper thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references behind it.
Have an independent reviewer who performed no part of the sampled testing sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Board Risk Committee reporting date exists in the repository.
